claims.statement: The runtime is a set of cooperating processes: a FastAPI backend served by `uvicorn src.main:app`, a Huey worker started as `huey_consumer src.worker.huey -w 2 --worker-type thread --periodic`, a SvelteKit SSR frontend, a stateless Go indicator-service sidecar, plus PostgreSQL 18, Redis 7 and mailcrab; the backend and worker each depend on postgres, redis and mailcrab, while the frontend depends on backend and worker.

The Go indicator sidecar is a stateless calculator with no authentication and no rate limiting, exposing only GET /health and POST /compute, and it is intended to be reachable only on the internal Docker network.

`src/main.py` builds the FastAPI app with `lifespan=lifespan_context`; the lifespan runs Alembic `upgrade(head)` in a worker thread when `settings.environment != "test"`, creates a fresh `svcs.Registry` stored on `app.state.svcs_registry`, calls `register_services(registry, sessionmanager)`, initializes the WebSocket manager Redis client/listener, and initializes the Huey worker dashboard with signal binding.

Lifespan teardown closes the Huey worker dashboard, the WebSocket manager and the Redis manager, and the lifespan body wraps its yield in a try/except so a failure during yield is logged instead of aborting shutdown.

The app is constructed with `debug=settings.environment != "prod"`, and in `dev` the module calls `debugpy.listen(("0.0.0.0", 5678))` at import time, which is why Docker Compose publishes a backend debug port.

HTTP API routes live under `/api/v1`: `src/main.py` creates one `APIRouter(prefix="/api/v1")`, includes the account, portfolio, auth, institutions, integration and market domain routers into it, and mounts it on the app; domain routers define their own segment on top of that (for example `auth_router` is `APIRouter(prefix="/auth")` and `market_router` is `APIRouter(prefix="/market")`), so older documentation describing bare `/api` paths without the `/v1` segment is inaccurate.

Apart from `/api/v1`, the app's top-level routes are the WebSocket endpoint `/api/ws`, the ad-hoc `/api/ping`, `/health/live` and `/health/ready` defined in `src/main.py`, and the Huey worker dashboard mounted at prefix `/worker/api` (task routes under `/worker/api/tasks` and a dashboard WebSocket at `/worker/api/updates`).

`/health/live` always returns `200 {"status": "alive"}` and is the probe used by the backend container healthcheck, while `/health/ready` checks a resolved `AsyncSession` with `select(1)` and pings Redis through `redis_manager.client()`, returning `200 {"status": "ready"}` only when every check is `ok` and `503 {"status": "degraded"}` otherwise.
`/api/ping` resolves an `AsyncSession`, runs `select(1)`, and returns `{"ping": "pong", "database": "ok"|"error"}`, reporting database failure in the response body instead of failing the request.

The middleware stack installed in `src/main.py` is `RequestIdMiddleware`, the slowapi rate-limit middleware plus a `reset_rate_limit_state_middleware` shim, the `cors_exception_middleware` safety net, and `CORSMiddleware`; because Starlette applies middleware in reverse order of `add_middleware`, `RequestIdMiddleware` is outermost.

`RequestIdMiddleware` reads an incoming `X-Request-ID` or generates a UUID, stores it on `request.state` and in a contextvar for log correlation, echoes it on the response, and logs one line per request with `duration_ms` at `warning` level for 4xx and `info` otherwise.

Rate limiting uses slowapi keyed by a `user_or_ip_key_func` that decodes the user id from the `auth_token` cookie or `authorization` header JWT and falls back to the remote address, with Redis (`settings.redis_url`) as storage outside `test` and `memory://` in tests.

`cors_exception_middleware` catches exceptions that escape the normal FastAPI handlers and returns a `500` JSON response while re-injecting CORS headers for allowed origins; `CORSMiddleware` is configured from comma-split `cors_allow_origins`/`cors_allow_methods`/`cors_allow_headers` and, outside `prod`, additionally allows `allow_origin_regex=r"https?://.*"`.

`src/main.py` registers global exception handlers that map `EntityNotFoundError` and `AuthorizationError` to `404` with an `{"error": ...}` body (deliberately hiding existence from unauthorized callers) and any other `Exception` to `500`, where the error detail is the exception string outside `prod` and the literal `"Internal Error"` in `prod`; the two domain handlers log nothing at all in `prod`, while outside `prod` they log `str(error)` / `error.log_message()` with `exc_info` in `dev`. `RateLimitExceeded` is routed to slowapi's `_rate_limit_exceeded_handler`.

Dependency injection is centralized in `src/config/services.py::register_services(registry, sessionmanager)`, shared by the API process and the worker: it registers `AsyncSession` as a factory over `sessionmanager.session`, registers core services, always registers account and auth services, and selects stub or live registration functions for the market and integration domains based on `settings.stub_external_api`.

Each backend domain owns its registrations in a `register_*_services(registry)` function (`src/core/registry.py`, `src/account/registry.py`, `src/auth/__init__.py`, `src/integration/registry.py`, `src/market/__init__.py`), so a new repository, service or domain API must be added there to be resolvable.

The Huey worker builds its own `svcs` registry in the `@huey.on_startup()` handler `setup_worker_services`, using a `DatabaseSessionManager` configured with `poolclass=NullPool` to avoid "operation in progress" errors across `asyncio.run()` task cycles, and stores it on `huey.svcs_registry`; tasks resolve services through `svcs.Container(huey.svcs_registry)`, and `@huey.on_shutdown()` closes the registry.

The worker uses `MemoryHuey` when `settings.environment == "test"` and `RedisHuey` (with `settings.redis_url`) otherwise, and imports `src/account/task.py`, `src/integration/task.py` and `src/market/task.py` at module bottom so their task decorators register.

Background work spans three task modules: `src/integration/task.py` syncs broker positions and emits WebSocket sync-progress events; `src/market/task.py` owns the on-demand `generate_note_title_task`, the periodic `daily_price_update` on `crontab(hour="0", minute="0")` and the periodic `hourly_intraday_price_update` on `crontab(minute="0")`, which fans out to `recalculate_all_account_totals_task` and `check_and_dispatch_price_alerts` (which in turn enqueues the `retries=3` `alert_email_dispatch_task`); and `src/account/task.py` exposes `recalculate_all_account_totals_task`, which recalculates account totals and pushes `AccountTotalsUpdatedMessage` per user. Tasks bridge synchronous Huey to async logic with `asyncio.run(...)` and re-bind the originating `request_id` into the contextvar.

`src/ws/manager.py` exposes a process-global `ConnectionManager` singleton holding `active_connections` per `UserId` and per-event-loop Redis clients in `_clients`; messages are published to the Redis Pub/Sub channel `ws_messages` and delivered to local connections by a background listener task, so Huey worker threads can fan out into the API process, and `send_personal_message` falls back to local broadcast when Redis is unavailable.

The `/api/ws` WebSocket endpoint authenticates either with a short-lived signed ticket (query parameter `ticket`, produced by `POST /api/v1/auth/ws-ticket` with `URLSafeTimedSerializer`, `salt="ws-ticket"` and `max_age=30`) or with a session token from the `auth_token` cookie or `sec-websocket-protocol` header resolved through `UserApi`, and closes with code `1008` when authentication fails.

WebSocket tickets are single-use: `_check_ticket_not_replayed` atomically sets a `ws-ticket-used:<sha256 of ticket>` key in Redis with `nx=True, ex=30` and the connection is closed with code `1008` on a detected replay; the worker dashboard's `/worker/api/updates` endpoint reuses the same helper.

The backend layer rules that hold across domains are: repositories always return schemas and never ORM models; cross-domain calls go only through the other domain's `api.py` APIs and `api_types.py`; routers own HTTP concerns while services must not raise `HTTPException` (the authorization service being the documented exception), with domain errors inheriting from `EntityNotFoundError`/`AuthorizationError`; services are registered as factories and resolved from the registry rather than instantiated by hand; and editing a model requires an Alembic migration named `<hash>_<description>.py`.

Route handlers receive the `svcs` container as a FastAPI dependency (`DepContainer`) and resolve collaborators by interface, for example `api = await services.aget(AccountApi)`; the frontend talks to the backend through the same `/api/v1` base, using `VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL` for SSR loads and `VITE_API_BASE_URL` for browser calls, and `JWT_SECRET` is derived from the backend `SECRET_KEY` for the SSR route guard.

`frontend/src/hooks.server.ts` is the SSR route guard: it verifies the `auth_token` cookie as an HS256 JWT with `JWT_SECRET`, deletes the cookie and drops `locals.user` when verification fails or the `scope` claim is not `access`, redirects unauthenticated non-`/auth` visitors to `/auth/login` with status `303`, and redirects an authenticated visitor away from `/auth/login` and `/auth/signup` back to `/`.

Background task modules are imported at the bottom of `src/worker.py` (`src/account/task.py`, `src/integration/task.py`, `src/market/task.py`) so their Huey task decorators register, which means a new task module must be added to that import list to be picked up by the consumer.
